# See below for a complete multi-format configuration example.

# configured correctly (e.g., LaTeX packages for PDF rendering).
metadata-files:
  - ./_include/author.yml
  - ./_include/format.pdf.yml
  - ./_include/format.html.yml
format:
  html: {}
  pdf: {}
# Metadata files are merged into page frontmatter at render time.
# Use this for shared author info, format overrides, etc.
# metadata-files:
#   - ./_include/author.yml
#   - ./_include/format.pdf.yml
# Bibliography file for citations (BibTeX format).
# bibliography: references.bib
# Enable link citations in the HTML output.
# link-citations: true
# Enable colored hyperlinks (works for both HTML and PDF output).
# colorlinks: true
---

Welcome to the SDBS Documentation Build System. This platform manages the
end-to-end rendering pipeline for Quarto-based documentation projects, from
source discovery through parallel rendering to multi-format output. SDBS
handles caching, dependency tracking, and profile-based configuration so that
documentation authors focus on content rather than build orchestration.

## Build System Features

### Parallel Rendering

SDBS renders multiple Quarto documents concurrently, using physical CPU cores
for optimal throughput. The worker pool size is configurable via `build.yml`.
Documents with no dependencies on each other are scheduled in parallel; the
dependency graph is resolved before any render begins.

### Intelligent Caching

Each document is content-addressed by a hash of its source text, included
fragments, and configuration. SDBS skips rendering for documents whose hash
matches the previous build. Modifying an included fragment triggers rebuilds
only for documents that actually include it. Cache entries are stored in
`.sdb_cache` by default.

### External Configuration

Build parameters are externalized in `build.yml`, which supports:

- **Target-specific overrides**: Set per-file or per-glob format options, PDF
  LaTeX headers, and output directories.
- **Exclusion patterns**: Prevent draft or archive files from being included
  in the build.
- **Profiles**: Define `local`, `ci`, or custom profiles to control caching
  behavior, link checking, and output cleaning per environment.

### Multi-Format Output

Each target can produce multiple output formats in a single build pass. Common
format combinations include:

- `html` only (default, fastest for iteration)
- `html + pdf` (website with downloadable print copies)
- `html + pdf + docx` (full distribution)

Format-specific overrides (LaTeX packages, CSS, include-in-header) are applied
per target, allowing fine-grained control without duplicating source files.

### C2PA Provenance (Optional)

Selected outputs can be signed with C2PA manifests, providing cryptographic
proof of authorship and content integrity. Enable this per target in
`build.yml`:

```yaml
targets:
  - path: "release/*.qmd"
    format:
      - html
      - pdf
    c2pa:
      enabled: true
      manifest: "./_c2pa/manifest.json"
```

### Website-Mode Isolation

For website profiles, each target is rendered in a fully isolated temporary
directory, preventing resource conflicts between concurrent renders and
enabling true parallel website generation.

## Build and Contribute

SDBS (SSCCS Documentation Build System) orchestrates Quarto renders with
intelligent caching and parallelism, enabling fast, reproducible builds of
multi-format outputs. It is designed to handle complex documentation projects
with many interdependent files while minimizing redundant work. All
documentation is written in plain Markdown (`.md` / `.qmd`) with YAML
frontmatter. The build is orchestrated by SDBS using
[Quarto](https://quarto.org).

### Environment Setup

Clone the SDBS repository and use the provided Docker environment for a
reproducible build state:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ssccsorg/sdbs.git
cd sdbs
docker build -t sdbs .
docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/docs:/workspace/docs sdbs
```

### Local Build (Without Docker)

A preconfigured DevContainer provides all dependencies pre-installed for
consistent development across platforms. Alternatively, install SDBS via pip:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ssccsorg/sdbs.git
cd sdbs
pip install .
sdbs-build /path/to/docs
```

### Quick Start

```bash
sdbs-build /path/to/docs           # generate all targets for local use
sdbs-build /path/to/docs --website  # generate website-optimized outputs
```

For other usage examples and a complete description of the system, see the
[SDBS repository](https://github.com/ssccsorg/sdbs).

### Docs Checker

SDBS includes a documentation validation tool (see the SDBS repository for
CLI usage):

- Links (local/remote, YAML frontmatter, BibTeX)
- Citations: reports if `@key` is missing from `.bib`, or if `.bib` is
  completely unused
